description: R55-C14: reconciliation responses may carry the canonical HLC head pair canonicalHlcWallMs/canonicalHlcCounter. When both are present Core uses the pair as the head that hides never-sent operations (delivery projection and the v3 display before and after); otherwise it keeps serverHlcWallMs/serverHlcCounter. `before` is the stack (R55-C11) envelope, `expected` the fixed one. user rows: a never-sent Start older than serverHlc* but newer than the canonical pair, hidden before and projected now. other rows: the canonical pair is not older than the Start, so it stays hidden, byte-identical. fallback rows carry no pair, byte-identical. error rows: one field only, canonical above server, or a value that is not a JavaScript-safe non-negative integer; accepted before, refused now with `message`. clock rows: v1 clock rebasing stays on serverHlc*, so a valid pair changes nothing. -duration-after-acknowledged-barrier rows: a never-sent duration change behind an acknowledged duration row, which only the v3 display after the response can admit. -user-start-then-pause-order: a never-sent Start between the pair and the server HLC and a never-sent Pause newer than both; the display before and after the response share the head, so the stored projection-pending commands keep the local order. server rows: the pair is present and the server HLC is invalid (negative, above 2^53 - 1, or 2^53 - 1 itself, which fails the clock-skew check); the error names the server HLC, as it does without the pair.
